project.name: OOP Primary Care opening
project.brief: Out of Pocket is expanding, fast, and is now running more big projects at once than any newsletter company should. This is one of them. OOP is opening OOP Primary Care: 3 clinics and 25 new doctors and nurse practitioners. Before a provider can see patients and bill insurance, someone has to verify their license and training and enroll them with every insurance company. That's called credentialing. The clinics open Tuesday, Nov 10, and 1,100 appointments are already booked, so the date is not moving. The project tracker says things are mostly on track. Your job is to figure out what's really going on before opening day

notes.title: Opening day readiness
bullets: Dr. Brenner opened with 15 minutes on the care model. No questions
Enrollments, billing IDs, and leases: Rosa is waiting on Tomas, Tomas is waiting on Gwen, Gwen is waiting on Rosa. Gwen asked everyone to "parallel path it"

Rosa owns credentialing profiles, insurance enrollments, hospital privileges, and malpractice certificates for 25 providers. She left after 5 minutes to call back an insurance company that has had her on hold since Tuesday
Credentialing profiles: 90% done. The last 10% is 6 providers who haven't signed their attestations
Records system: Wade says on track. Dr. Brenner asked what "EPCS identity proofing" means. Wade said it's "mostly paperwork"
Tomas asked what happens if providers aren't credentialed by opening day. The ticket says TBD. It was due Oct 2
Nobody is calling booked patients to check their insurance before their appointments. Nobody owns it
Two sets of provider bios are being written, Jules's and Gwen's. Agreed to "pick the best one"
The credentialing software is still assigned to Kurt, whose contract ended in June. Rosa is tracking everything in a spreadsheet
Opening day stays Nov 10. 1,100 appointments are booked
